hook.text: Its futuristic Thailand is portrayed as a simulation city, a concept from within the musician that Thailand inspired.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: August 1994 to March 1995, in Yokohama, Karuizawa, Bangkok and Tokyo

sentences.text: In 1994 his neighbour, Doll Magazine editor-in-chief Mikio Moriwaki, suggested he try a Pink Floyd-style sound for his next record.
The first plan was a '90s take on The Dark Side of the Moon, covering much the same ground as Virtual Rabbit.
Later, he came up with the World Inspection Tour, a role-playing game held overseas for members of his fan club, Hirasawa Bypass.
The tour was set for Phuket in Thailand, since the flight was short and the place had little Japanese tourism.
On that trial visit he had no clear idea, only a rough picture of the Vietnam War.
One night at the Simon Cabaret, where every performer was kathoey, shaped how he saw Thai culture.
Hirasawa did not trust the Thai studio with his gear, so he brought only instrumental 24-track recordings on analog reels to Thailand.
There he recorded only vocals over four days, his own and those of Thai performers.
Although he was not fluent in Thai, he wrote some lyrics by cross-referencing four language guidebooks.
What he first wrote meant something other than he intended, so he rewrote lyrics and melodies on the spot.
Masanori Chinzei handled recording and mixing, and Keiko Ueda mastered it.
The booklet was shot in Thailand, and it is the only one of his solo albums where he is not the only person pictured.
It was his fifth studio album and his last record with Polydor.
He later switched labels to Nippon Columbia.

listen_for.text: Miss N. of the Phuket Simon Cabaret narrates it, and its lyrics are by her and Hirasawa.
Wisakha Fraytes sings on it, and Miss N. narrates it without a credit.
Miss N. narrates this track as well.
